column1: # TRAIT NEIGHBOURS — the lookup for FACETS.md step 1.
# Why this file exists. The near-neighbour collision is the most expensive failure in
# step 4: a scene gets built, then thrown away because it belongs to a trait somebody
# already wrote. It cannot be computed from the axes — hard-line (kidney/bitter/fried)
# and firm (navy/sour/dried) share no bean, no flavour and no form, and mystical sits
# next to otherworldly across a single shared form. So the adjacency was worked out by
# hand, once, over all 360 traits, rather than re-derived in every batch.
# How to use it. At step 1, look your five up here and READ the entries listed, then
# write the separation prose into the batch file as before — what each neighbour owns,
# and what is left for yours. This file names the pairs; it does not do the thinking,
# and it is not a substitute for reading beans/, flavours/ and forms/.
# Neighbours are ordered by collision risk:
#   trait(slug)    already written — its five scenes are SPENT, go and read them
#   ~trait(slug)   not yet written — no scenes to avoid, but the axes must still part
#   !trait(slug)   not yet written AND IN YOUR OWN BATCH — the worst case, because two
#                  entries written in one sitting collapse into each other silently
# Rebuild after a batch: the written/unwritten marks go stale. Regenerate or hand-edit.
